events.name: Funding & Assumption Act
events.desc: Hamilton nationalizes Revolutionary War debt; federal assumption of state debts — births the national debt as a permanent monetary institution.

leadup.label: Treasury Department created
leadup.note: Hamilton named Secretary; the looming debt-assumption fight intensifies

leadup.label: Public securities double in three months
leadup.note: speculation surges on the prospect of federal redemption at par

leadup.label: Hamilton's First Report on Public Credit
leadup.note: proposes funding the federal debt and assuming the states' war debts

leadup.label: Madison's 'discrimination' plan defeated
leadup.note: House refuses to pay original holders separately from speculators

leadup.label: House rejects assumption, 31-29
leadup.note: Virginia-led opposition stalls Hamilton's plan

leadup.label: The dinner-table bargain
leadup.note: Jefferson hosts Hamilton & Madison; capital-for-assumption deal struck

leadup.label: Residence Act signed (capital to the Potomac)
leadup.note: half the bargain — the seat of government moves south

leadup.label: Assumption passes the House
leadup.note: four Potomac-state votes switch; Hamilton's plan narrowly clears

entity_action.label: Births the national debt
entity_action.note: Hamilton nationalizes Revolutionary War debt — the first permanent federal liability is itself an entity on the sovereign's balance sheet.

events.name: First Bank of the United States chartered
events.desc: First central bank; 20-yr charter. Buildup: Bank of North America 1781 -> Report on Public Credit Jan 1790 -> charter.

leadup.label: Bank of North America chartered
leadup.note: Robert Morris's wartime bank, first national bank under the Confederation

leadup.label: Hamilton's First Report on Public Credit
leadup.note: assumption and funding of the debt — fiscal groundwork for a bank

leadup.label: Compromise of 1790 (debt assumption passes)
leadup.note: Funding Act trades the capital site for assumption, clearing the path

leadup.label: Hamilton's Report on a National Bank
leadup.note: proposes a $10M central bank with a 20-year charter

leadup.label: Bank bill passes the Senate
leadup.note: first chamber approval

leadup.label: Bank bill passes the House
leadup.note: sent to Washington amid Madison's constitutional objections

leadup.label: Hamilton's opinion on bank constitutionality
leadup.note: implied-powers defense persuades Washington over Jefferson & Randolph

entity_action.label: First government bank chartered
entities: First Bank of the United States
entity_action.note: First government-sponsored banking corporation. 20-year charter, $10M capitalization. The template for every central-bank chartering to follow.

events.name: Coinage Act / U.S. Mint
events.desc: Defines the dollar; bimetallic (gold+silver) standard; the original monetary constitution.

leadup.label: Robert Morris proposes a national mint
leadup.note: the Superintendent of Finance urges a federal coinage and a decimal unit

leadup.label: Jefferson's 'Notes on Coinage'
leadup.note: argues for the Spanish dollar as the unit, divided decimally

leadup.label: Congress adopts the dollar as the unit
leadup.note: the Confederation Congress votes the decimal dollar into being

leadup.label: Confederation Congress passes a mint ordinance
leadup.note: establishes a mint on paper, though no coins follow under the Articles

leadup.label: Hamilton's Report on the Establishment of a Mint
leadup.note: recommends a 15:1 gold-silver bimetallic standard

leadup.label: First Bank chartered; public-credit machinery set
leadup.note: the institutional stage for a federal coinage is in place

entity_action.label: US Mint chartered
entity_action.note: Charters the Mint as a Treasury bureau — operational to this day. Defines the dollar in metal.

events.name: First Bank charter dies
events.desc: Congress refuses recharter by one vote; the nation enters the War of 1812 with no central bank — finance chaos follows.

leadup.label: First Bank chartered for a 20-year term
leadup.note: Hamilton's bank wins a charter set to expire in 1811

leadup.label: Jefferson's opposition put on the record
leadup.note: he calls the Bank unconstitutional — the seed of the recharter fight

leadup.label: Bank petitions Congress early for recharter
leadup.note: stockholders apply well ahead of the charter's expiry

leadup.label: Gallatin's report urges renewal
leadup.note: the Treasury Secretary backs the Bank as fiscally essential

leadup.label: States'-rights & foreign-ownership attacks mount
leadup.note: ~70% of shares held abroad inflames the opposition

leadup.label: House tables the recharter bill by one vote
leadup.note: effectively kills renewal; a Senate tie seals it in February

entity_action.label: First Bank dissolved
entities: First Bank of the United States
entity_action.note: Death by non-renewal: Congress refuses recharter by one vote. The nation enters a war with no central bank.

events.name: Second Bank of the United States
events.desc: Post-war inflation & state-bank chaos force a new central bank. 20-yr charter.

leadup.label: First Bank charter expires (not renewed)
leadup.note: Senate killed recharter, leaving no central bank entering the war

leadup.label: War of 1812 declared
leadup.note: war finance strains a Treasury with no national bank

leadup.label: Banks suspend specie payments
leadup.note: after Washington is burned, banks outside New England stop redeeming notes

leadup.label: Dallas report urges a national bank
leadup.note: new Treasury Sec. recommends a second Bank to fund the Treasury

leadup.label: Madison vetoes the 1815 bank bill
leadup.note: objects the proposed bank wouldn't aid wartime credit

leadup.label: Calhoun introduces the new bank bill
leadup.note: Republican nationalists Calhoun & Clay drive the $35M charter

leadup.label: Bank bill passes the House, 80-71
leadup.note: narrow approval sends it to Madison

entity_action.label: Second Bank chartered
entities: Second Bank of the United States
entity_action.note: Re-chartering: new entity, same role, different articles. Born from wartime finance chaos.

events.name: Jackson's Bank War / veto
events.desc: Jackson vetoes recharter; removes federal deposits 1833; Specie Circular 1836 -> charter dies 1836 -> Panic of 1837. The populist money war.

leadup.label: Jackson's first message attacks the Bank
leadup.note: questions its constitutionality years before recharter is due

leadup.label: Jackson renews Bank criticism in 2nd message
leadup.note: floats a Treasury-run alternative, escalating tension with Biddle

leadup.label: Biddle files early recharter bill
leadup.note: Clay's strategy forces the issue in an election year, 4 years early

leadup.label: Recharter bill passes both houses
leadup.note: Congress sends the recharter to Jackson

leadup.label: Taney named Treasury Sec. to remove deposits
leadup.note: after firing Duane, Jackson installs Taney to pull federal funds

leadup.label: Federal deposits moved to 'pet banks'
leadup.note: Biddle contracts credit in response, deepening the war

leadup.label: Senate censures Jackson, 26-20
leadup.note: Clay-led Senate condemns the deposit removal

leadup.label: Specie Circular issued
leadup.note: land payments required in gold & silver, tightening money

leadup.label: Panic of 1837 / specie suspension
leadup.note: banks suspend payments weeks into Van Buren's term

entity_action.label: Second Bank killed
entities: Second Bank of the United States
entity_action.note: Entity death by presidential act. Jackson vetoes recharter, removes deposits to 'pet banks.' The populist money war.

events.name: Legal Tender Act — the Greenbacks
events.desc: Civil War finance: fiat paper money to fund the Union; first national paper currency not backed by specie on demand.

leadup.label: Civil War begins (Fort Sumter)
leadup.note: immediate demand for unprecedented war finance

leadup.label: Demand Notes authorized
leadup.note: $50M in notes redeemable in specie 'on demand'

leadup.label: Revenue Act of 1861 (first income tax)
leadup.note: 3% over $800, to fund the war

leadup.label: Banks & Treasury suspend specie payments
leadup.note: breaks the promise to redeem Demand Notes, forcing new money

leadup.label: Chase report floats a national currency
leadup.note: Treasury's annual report seeds the national banking plan

leadup.label: Spaulding's legal-tender bill in the House
leadup.note: Ways & Means drives the greenback bill through debate

leadup.label: Revenue Act of 1862 (creates the IRS)
leadup.note: Commissioner of Internal Revenue to service war debt

leadup.label: National Currency Act introduced in Senate
leadup.note: Chase & Sen. John Sherman push a national bank system

entity_action.label: Treasury balance sheet restructured
entity_action.note: Creates a new class of obligation (greenbacks) without a new entity — restructures the Treasury's own balance sheet.

events.name: National Banking Act
events.desc: Creates national banks + a uniform national currency; taxes state notes out of existence. The wartime banking standard.

leadup.label: NY/Boston/Phila banks suspend specie
leadup.note: the wartime gold standard breaks, forcing a new kind of money

leadup.label: Chase recommends a national currency
leadup.note: the Treasury's annual report seeds the national-bank plan

leadup.label: Legal Tender Act creates the greenbacks
leadup.note: $150M in fiat notes — but they sag against gold, spurring reform

leadup.label: Greenback dollar falls to 91 cents in gold
leadup.note: depreciation drives the case for bond-backed national banks

leadup.label: Sherman & Chase push the bill in the Senate
leadup.note: the National Currency bill advances over state-bank resistance

leadup.label: Senate passes the National Currency bill, 23-21
leadup.note: a narrow win sends it on to the House

entity_action.label: Mass chartering — OCC + national banks
entities: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
entity_action.note: Mass chartering: creates the OCC (the entity that charters other entities) + an entire class of nationally chartered banks. The OCC was born ON the chartering degree (21° Libra).

events.name: Coinage Act of 1873 — 'Crime of '73'
events.desc: Demonetizes silver -> de facto gold standard. Railroad-finance bubble bursts Sept 1873 (Jay Cooke) -> the Long Depression.

leadup.label: Public Credit Act of 1869 signed
leadup.note: commits the government to redeem Civil War bonds in coin, opening the road to gold

leadup.label: Knox report codifying the mint laws
leadup.note: ~100-page consolidation of coinage statutes as the basis for the new bill

leadup.label: Knox draft proposes dropping the silver dollar
leadup.note: recommends eliminating the standard silver dollar from coinage

leadup.label: Senate passes first coinage bill, 36-14
leadup.note: the House never takes it up before the Congress expires

leadup.label: House passes Hooper substitute, 110-13
leadup.note: passes with almost no debate and without being read aloud

leadup.label: Senate passes reworked bill; trade dollar added
leadup.note: Sherman manages final passage; conference settles differences

leadup.label: Jay Cooke & Co. fails; Panic of 1873
leadup.note: collapse over Northern Pacific financing forces a 10-day NYSE closure

entity_action.label: Mint mandate restructured
entity_action.note: Demonetizes silver, restructuring the Mint's mandate from bimetallic to de facto gold.

events.name: Resumption of Specie Payments
events.desc: Greenbacks made convertible to gold again; the U.S. returns to hard money after the war/Reconstruction inflation.

leadup.label: Public Credit Act pledges coin redemption
leadup.note: commits the US to pay its bonds in gold — the road to resumption

leadup.label: Coinage Act of 1873 ('Crime of '73')
leadup.note: drops the silver dollar, hardening the money toward gold

leadup.label: Panic of 1873 / Jay Cooke fails
leadup.note: the Long Depression stiffens the contraction-vs-greenback fight

leadup.label: Resumption Act sets a Jan 1 1879 target
leadup.note: a lame-duck Congress pledges to redeem greenbacks in specie

leadup.label: Greenback Party nominates Peter Cooper
leadup.note: a soft-money revolt against the resumption course

leadup.label: Bland-Allison silver coinage, over a veto
leadup.note: forces monthly silver buys — a partial inflationist counterstroke

leadup.label: Gold premium vanishes for the first time since 1861
leadup.note: Sherman's gold buildup brings parity within reach

entity_action.label: Treasury liability restructured
entity_action.note: Greenbacks made redeemable in gold — restructures the Treasury's relationship to its own paper.

events.name: Panic of 1893 / Silver repeal
events.desc: Railroad over-build + gold drain -> severe depression; Sherman Silver Purchase Act repealed Nov 1893. Gold vs silver politics peak.

leadup.label: Sherman Silver Purchase Act
leadup.note: forces big monthly silver buys that steadily drain Treasury gold

leadup.label: Baring Panic rattles world credit
leadup.note: London's near-failure tightens money and pulls gold from New York

leadup.label: Philadelphia & Reading Railroad fails
leadup.note: a $125M bankruptcy lights the fuse amid gold-reserve fears

leadup.label: Treasury gold falls below the $100M floor
leadup.note: the legal reserve breaks, stoking fear of suspended payments

leadup.label: National Cordage collapses
leadup.note: the trust's failure sets the panic ablaze; the market craters the next day

leadup.label: ~600 banks and 15,000 firms begin to fail
leadup.note: a 'currency famine' forces scrip and certified checks into use

leadup.label: Cleveland convenes a special session
leadup.note: summons Congress to repeal the Sherman Act and stop the gold drain

entity_action.label: Triggers silver repeal
entity_action.note: Market event that triggers entity action at the next break. Railroad over-build + gold drain; Sherman Silver Purchase Act repealed.

events.name: Bryan 'Cross of Gold'
events.desc: Free-silver populism vs the gold standard reaches its rhetorical climax; the money question becomes THE national fight.

leadup.label: Bryan's three-hour anti-goldbug speech
leadup.note: the young Nebraskan emerges as the silver tribune

leadup.label: Sherman Silver Purchase Act repealed
leadup.note: Cleveland's gold-wing victory splits the Democratic Party

leadup.label: Coxey's Army marches on Washington
leadup.note: depression desperation pours into the silver-vs-gold politics

leadup.label: Morgan-Belmont syndicate rescues the Treasury
leadup.note: private bankers supply gold for bonds — a lightning rod for resentment

leadup.label: $100M gold-bond issue; Morgan takes $62M
leadup.note: another banker-led rescue inflames the free-silver revolt

leadup.label: Democratic convention opens in Chicago
leadup.note: silver delegates seize control of the platform fight

entity_action.label: Political — no entity action
entity_action.note: The money question as pure politics. No entity is created, killed, or restructured — but the fight sets the stage for 1900.

events.name: Gold Standard Act
events.desc: Gold formally made the single standard; closes the bimetallic era.

leadup.label: Panic of 1893 breaks on Wall Street
leadup.note: markets crash, draining Treasury gold and igniting the money fight

leadup.label: Sherman Silver Purchase Act repealed
leadup.note: repeals the silver mandate to stem the gold drain, splitting the Democrats

leadup.label: Morgan-Belmont gold-bond Treasury rescue
leadup.note: ~$62M bond contract refills gold reserves below the $100M floor

leadup.label: Bryan's 'Cross of Gold' speech
leadup.note: rallies delegates for free silver and wins the nomination

leadup.label: McKinley defeats Bryan (gold vs silver)
leadup.note: settles the currency question at the polls

leadup.label: Indianapolis Monetary Convention convenes
leadup.note: boards of trade authorize a private commission to draft a gold plan

leadup.label: Indianapolis Monetary Commission report
leadup.note: recommends a statutory gold standard and asset-based bank currency

leadup.label: Gold Standard bill passes the House
leadup.note: the new 56th Congress quickly passes the financial bill

entity_action.label: Standard codified
entity_action.note: Codifies what was already practice — gold as the single standard. Closes the bimetallic era.

events.name: Panic of 1907
events.desc: Banker-led (Morgan) rescue exposes the lack of a lender of last resort -> drives the campaign for a central bank.

leadup.label: San Francisco earthquake drains capital/gold
leadup.note: insurance payouts pull gold to the US, tightening credit into 1907

leadup.label: United Copper corner collapses (Heinze/Morse)
leadup.note: the failed corner triggers runs on associated banks

leadup.label: Knickerbocker Trust suspends after a run
leadup.note: pays ~$8M in hours then suspends, igniting the panic

leadup.label: Treasury adds $25M; Morgan rescues call money
leadup.note: Morgan raises ~$23.6M to keep the NYSE open as rates spike

leadup.label: Moore & Schley / TC&I rescue at Morgan's library
leadup.note: US Steel buys Tennessee Coal & Iron to save the brokerage

leadup.label: Clearinghouse certificates retired; panic ends
leadup.note: last loan certificates retired, marking full resolution

entity_action.label: Triggers the Fed
entity_action.note: The panic that proves the need for a lender of last resort. Triggers the National Monetary Commission → Jekyll Island → the Federal Reserve Act (1913).

events.name: Federal Reserve Act
events.desc: Creates the Fed. Buildup: 1907 Panic -> National Monetary Commission -> Jekyll Island 1910 (Aldrich Plan) -> 1913. Also 16th Amendment income tax (Feb 1913).

leadup.label: Panic of 1907 — Knickerbocker collapses
leadup.note: exposes the lack of an elastic currency & lender of last resort

leadup.label: Aldrich-Vreeland Act signed
leadup.note: emergency currency act; creates the National Monetary Commission

leadup.label: National Monetary Commission established
leadup.note: chaired by Sen. Aldrich to study banking and recommend reform

leadup.label: Secret Jekyll Island meeting begins
leadup.note: Aldrich, Warburg, Vanderlip, Davison meet secretly to draft a plan

leadup.label: Aldrich Plan unveiled to the Commission
leadup.note: proposes a privately controlled National Reserve Association

leadup.label: Commission's final report to Congress
leadup.note: submits the report and draft National Reserve Association bill

leadup.label: Pujo 'money trust' hearings open
leadup.note: House subcommittee under Pujo, counsel Untermyer, probes Wall Street

leadup.label: J.P. Morgan testifies before the Pujo Committee
leadup.note: dramatizes banker control of credit — the 'money trust'

leadup.label: Pujo Committee report issued
leadup.note: finds a 'vast and growing concentration of control of money & credit'

leadup.label: Wilson's address to Congress on banking reform
leadup.note: urges a government-supervised reserve system, backing Glass-Owen

leadup.label: House passes the Glass-Owen bill, 287-85
leadup.note: approves its Federal Reserve bill sponsored by Carter Glass

leadup.label: Senate passes its version, 54-34
leadup.note: sends it to conference to reconcile with the House

leadup.label: House adopts the conference report, 298-60
leadup.note: the reconciled Act clears the House one day before signing

entity_action.label: Fed chartered
entity_action.note: Charters the most complex entity in the stack: a public Board bolted to 12 private Reserve Banks owned by their member banks — the dashed line on the org tree.

events.name: The Great Crash
events.desc: Roaring-20s credit & margin boom collapses; onset of the Great Depression.

leadup.label: Florida land bubble bursts
leadup.note: a dress rehearsal for speculative mania and collapse

leadup.label: Fed cuts rates ('the cheap-money error')
leadup.note: easy credit fuels the late-1920s margin & stock boom

leadup.label: Fed reverses to tighten against speculation
leadup.note: too late to deflate the bubble gently

leadup.label: Benjamin Strong dies; the Fed splits
leadup.note: loses its steadying hand, left 'largely paralyzed' into 1929

leadup.label: Mini-crash & call-money panic
leadup.note: a warning tremor as margin lending peaks

leadup.label: Fed raises the rediscount rate to 6%
leadup.note: the tightening that finally pricks the bubble

leadup.label: Dow tops at 381 (the peak)
leadup.note: the high-water mark before the slide

leadup.label: Black Thursday — panic selling begins
leadup.note: first day of the crash on the NYSE

entity_action.label: Triggers New Deal entity reforms
entity_action.note: The crash that triggers the largest wave of entity creation since the Civil War — SEC, FDIC, FHA, Fannie Mae, the whole New Deal apparatus.

events.name: Gold confiscation (EO 6102) + Bank Holiday
events.desc: FDR seizes private gold; nationwide bank holiday Mar 6; gold clause abrogated; Glass-Steagall Jun 1933. The domestic gold break.

leadup.label: Black Tuesday — market collapse
leadup.note: ~16M shares dumped; confidence in banking erodes

leadup.label: Pecora hearings (Stock Exchange Practices) begin
leadup.note: Senate Banking & Currency Committee opens its inquiry into the crash

leadup.label: Ferdinand Pecora hired as chief counsel
leadup.note: reinvigorates the probe into the great bank exposés

leadup.label: Michigan declares state bank holiday
leadup.note: 8-day closure; bank runs cascade state to state

leadup.label: FDR inaugurated; all 48 states shut banks
leadup.note: the crisis peaks at the inauguration

leadup.label: FDR proclaims a national bank holiday
leadup.note: four-day nationwide closure until Congress can act

leadup.label: Emergency Banking Act signed
leadup.note: authorizes federal control over gold and bank reopenings

entity_action.label: Citizen-entity relationship restructured
entity_action.note: Restructures the citizen-to-money-entity relationship: gold confiscation = mandatory redemption. Glass-Steagall creates new walls between entity types.

events.name: Gold Reserve Act — dollar devalued
events.desc: Gold repriced $20.67 -> $35/oz; the Treasury takes the gold; a one-time 41% dollar devaluation.

leadup.label: Executive Order 6102 — gold confiscation
leadup.note: forbids private hoarding of gold coin, bullion, certificates

leadup.label: US effectively leaves the gold standard
leadup.note: FDR halts gold exports, letting the dollar float downward

leadup.label: Joint Resolution abrogates the gold clause
leadup.note: voids gold-payment clauses in public and private contracts

leadup.label: Glass-Steagall (Banking Act of 1933)
leadup.note: separates commercial/investment banking; creates the FDIC

leadup.label: RFC gold-buying program begins
leadup.note: Warren-Pearson theory: bid gold up to lift commodity prices

leadup.label: Managed gold price reaches ~$34/oz
leadup.note: up from ~$29 in October as the program drives the dollar down

entity_action.label: ESF chartered
entity_action.note: Charters the ESF — Treasury's emergency reserve, still standing. A new entity born from the gold repricing.

events.name: Bretton Woods
events.desc: Dollar-gold global system; IMF + World Bank; the dollar becomes the world's reserve currency. American monetary empire begins.

leadup.label: Atlantic Charter issued
leadup.note: FDR-Churchill declaration of postwar economic-cooperation aims

leadup.label: Keynes drafts British clearing-union plan
leadup.note: UK proposal for an International Clearing Union and 'bancor'

leadup.label: Harry Dexter White circulates US Treasury plan
leadup.note: rival 'White Plan' for a stabilization fund, gold-dollar anchored

leadup.label: Keynes Plan vs White Plan debated publicly
leadup.note: competing UK and US blueprints aired and negotiated

leadup.label: Anglo-American technical negotiations begin
leadup.note: experts start reconciling the two plans in Washington

leadup.label: Joint Statement of Experts on an IMF published
leadup.note: agreed Allied blueprint released simultaneously in capitals

leadup.label: Atlantic City preliminary drafting conference
leadup.note: 16+ nations pre-negotiate the text

leadup.label: Bretton Woods Conference convenes
leadup.note: 730 delegates from 44 nations open at Mount Washington Hotel

entity_action.label: Supranational tier chartered
entities: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
entity_action.note: Charters the supranational tier: IMF + IBRD (the whole World Bank Group). Both now at progressed Full Moon — the international order at crisis.

events.name: Nixon closes the gold window
events.desc: End of dollar-gold convertibility -> pure fiat. Buildup: 1960s gold drain, London Gold Pool collapse 1968, SDRs 1969, Triffin dilemma.

leadup.label: Triffin testifies to Congress on the dilemma
leadup.note: warns the world needs dollars but the dollar glut erodes gold backing

leadup.label: London Gold Pool formed by eight nations
leadup.note: central banks pool gold to defend the $35/oz price

leadup.label: Gold Pool collapses; two-tier market
leadup.note: a run on gold splits official and free-market prices

leadup.label: IMF creates Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
leadup.note: synthetic reserve asset to ease pressure on the dollar

leadup.label: West Germany floats the mark
leadup.note: early crack as dollar pressure mounts in Europe

leadup.label: Reuss subcommittee urges dollar devaluation
leadup.note: House report signals the peg is politically untenable

leadup.label: Nixon convenes his team at Camp David
leadup.note: secret weekend meeting to design the New Economic Policy

entity_action.label: Bretton Woods operating charter dissolved
entity_action.note: Dissolution of the system's operating charter — not the institutions (the IMF survives), but the original mandate dies. Pure fiat begins.

events.name: Oil shock / petrodollar / floating rates
events.desc: OPEC embargo + the shift to floating exchange rates (formalized Jamaica 1976); the dollar re-anchored to oil.

leadup.label: Nixon closes the gold window
leadup.note: ends dollar-gold convertibility — the dollar is now unanchored

leadup.label: Smithsonian Agreement devalues the dollar
leadup.note: a patched-up peg cuts the dollar ~8%, but it cannot hold

leadup.label: Second dollar devaluation (gold to $42/oz)
leadup.note: a further 10% cut as the peg keeps cracking

leadup.label: Generalized float ends the par-value system
leadup.note: major currencies float against the dollar — Bretton Woods is over

leadup.label: Yom Kippur War begins
leadup.note: the Arab-Israeli war sets up oil as a political weapon

leadup.label: OPEC unilaterally raises posted oil prices
leadup.note: Gulf states quadruple prices, routing petrodollars to Western banks

entity_action.label: Settlement system restructured
entity_action.note: OPEC embargo + floating rates restructure the international monetary settlement system. The dollar re-anchored to oil.

events.name: Volcker Shock
events.desc: Fed targets the money supply; rates to ~20% to break inflation. The monetarist turn; deep recession to reset the dollar.

leadup.label: Federal Reserve Reform Act of 1977
leadup.note: gives the Fed an explicit price-stability mandate as inflation climbs

leadup.label: Humphrey-Hawkins Full Employment Act
leadup.note: requires the Fed to report inflation & employment goals to Congress

leadup.label: Carter announces a dollar-rescue package
leadup.note: emergency measures as the dollar slides

leadup.label: Carter 'malaise' speech & cabinet shake-up
leadup.note: Miller moved to Treasury, opening the Fed chair

leadup.label: Volcker Senate confirmation hearing
leadup.note: inflation near 9% as the Banking Committee vets him

leadup.label: Volcker sworn in as Fed chairman
leadup.note: appointed to break inflation

leadup.label: FOMC raises discount rate on a split 4-3 vote
leadup.note: narrow vote signals the old approach is failing

entity_action.label: Fed operating method restructured
entity_action.note: Restructures the Fed's operating charter: targets reserves, not rates. America at 21.11° Libra — the chartering degree, third visit.

events.name: Plaza Accord
events.desc: Coordinated G5 dollar devaluation; managed-currency era; (Louvre 1987 + Black Monday Oct 1987 follow).

leadup.label: Volcker's high-rate regime begins
leadup.note: tight money to break inflation starts driving the dollar sharply up

leadup.label: US trade deficit hits a record
leadup.note: the soaring dollar guts US exporters and farm exports

leadup.label: James Baker becomes Treasury Secretary
leadup.note: abandons hands-off policy, moving to talk the dollar down

leadup.label: The dollar peaks (~+50% since 1980)
leadup.note: mark and yen near record lows; overvaluation becomes untenable

leadup.label: Congress presses protectionist trade bills
leadup.note: tariff threats push the G5 toward coordinated action

leadup.label: G5 ministers gather quietly at the Plaza
leadup.note: deputies finalize a plan to drive the dollar down by joint intervention

entity_action.label: Informal international restructuring
entity_action.note: Coordinated G5 dollar devaluation. Informal restructuring — no entities created or killed, but the managed-currency era begins.

events.name: Glass-Steagall repeal (Gramm-Leach-Bliley)
events.desc: Commercial + investment banking re-merged; the deregulation that enabled 2000s portfolio/derivative complexity.

leadup.label: Fed raises Section 20 revenue limit to 25%
leadup.note: loosens Glass-Steagall for bank securities affiliates

leadup.label: Citicorp-Travelers merger announced
leadup.note: $70B deal violates Glass-Steagall, betting Congress will change the law

leadup.label: Fed-led LTCM bailout
leadup.note: hedge-fund rescue amid the modernization debate

leadup.label: Senate passes S.900 (Gramm bill)
leadup.note: Senate version of Financial Services Modernization advances

leadup.label: House passes its modernization bill
leadup.note: sets up conference negotiations

leadup.label: House-Senate conference deal reached
leadup.note: final compromise on privacy & CRA clears the path

leadup.label: Congress passes Gramm-Leach-Bliley
leadup.note: Senate 90-8, House 362-57

entity_action.label: Entity-type walls removed
entity_action.note: Removes the wall between entity types: bank holding companies can now own securities firms. A deconsolidation — entities that were separate can now merge.

events.name: Dot-com peak / bust
events.desc: Nasdaq tops; the tech/credit bubble bursts -> the Greenspan-put easing that seeds the housing bubble.

leadup.label: Netscape IPO ignites the internet boom
leadup.note: a profitless firm doubles on day one, opening the dot-com era

leadup.label: Telecommunications Act of 1996
leadup.note: deregulation feeds a telecom/internet buildout and a capital rush

leadup.label: Greenspan warns of 'irrational exuberance'
leadup.note: the Fed chair flags overvaluation — the market shrugs and climbs

leadup.label: LTCM bailout, then the Fed cuts rates
leadup.note: easy money after the hedge-fund rescue re-fuels the bubble

leadup.label: Fed begins raising rates
leadup.note: the first of six hikes that will eventually prick the bubble

leadup.label: AOL-Time Warner merger announced
leadup.note: the $165B deal marks the manic top of internet valuations

entity_action.label: No direct entity action
entity_action.note: Nasdaq tops and crashes. No direct entity event — but the Greenspan-put easing seeds the housing bubble that will detonate in 2008.

events.name: Lehman / Global Financial Crisis
events.desc: Securitized-mortgage complexity detonates; TARP Oct 2008; QE1 + ZIRP. The post-gold system's near-death + the QE era begins.

leadup.label: Two Bear Stearns subprime funds collapse
leadup.note: first major sign the mortgage market is unraveling

leadup.label: BNP Paribas freezes funds; credit seizes
leadup.note: interbank funding stress marks the crisis onset

leadup.label: Bear Stearns sold to JPMorgan with Fed backing
leadup.note: fire-sale rescue financed by the Fed

leadup.label: Housing & Economic Recovery Act creates FHFA
leadup.note: sets up the regulator that will seize Fannie & Freddie

leadup.label: Fannie & Freddie put into conservatorship
leadup.note: FHFA takes over the mortgage giants

leadup.label: Fed bails out AIG with $85B credit line
leadup.note: insurer rescue as money markets break the buck

leadup.label: Paulson & Bernanke testify to Senate Banking
leadup.note: administration presses Congress for the $700B TARP

entity_action.label: Triggers Dodd-Frank mass chartering
entity_action.note: The near-death that triggers the next mass chartering. TARP is itself a temporary entity — created and wound down.

events.name: Dodd-Frank
events.desc: Post-crisis banking standard overhaul; the regulatory response.

leadup.label: TARP enacted amid the crash
leadup.note: the $700B bailout crystallizes the 'never again' reform demand

leadup.label: Obama unveils a financial-reform white paper
leadup.note: proposes the deepest regulatory overhaul since the 1930s

leadup.label: House passes the Wall Street Reform Act
leadup.note: first chamber clears H.R. 4173

leadup.label: SEC sues Goldman over the Abacus CDO
leadup.note: the fraud charge hardens the political case for reform

leadup.label: Senate passes its reform bill, 59-39
leadup.note: sends the measure to conference

leadup.label: House-Senate conference agrees final text
leadup.note: the reconciled Dodd-Frank bill heads for final passage

leadup.label: Senate clears the conference report, 60-39
leadup.note: final passage sends Dodd-Frank to the president

entity_action.label: Mass chartering — four new entities
entity_action.note: Mass chartering: four new entities in one statute. FSOC, OFR, CFPB, FIO. The post-crisis regulatory apparatus.

events.name: COVID — unlimited QE + CARES
events.desc: Fed backstops everything; CARES Act fiscal flood; the largest+fastest monetary expansion in U.S. history.

leadup.label: Repo market spikes; Fed re-enters
leadup.note: overnight rates surge, forcing the Fed back into the repo market

leadup.label: WHO declares COVID a global emergency
leadup.note: pandemic risk enters market & policy calculus

leadup.label: Stock market begins record-fast crash
leadup.note: fastest 30%+ drop from a peak in history

leadup.label: Fed emergency cut of 50bp
leadup.note: first unscheduled cut since 2008

leadup.label: Fed cuts to zero and restarts QE
leadup.note: Sunday emergency action plus $700B asset purchases

leadup.label: Fed revives commercial-paper & dealer facilities
leadup.note: 2008-era crisis tools relaunched

entity_action.label: Fed balance sheet + temporary entities
entity_action.note: Creates temporary entities (SIGPR, lending facilities) and restructures the Fed's balance sheet. The largest monetary expansion in US history.

events.name: TODAY — FedNow / GENIUS stablecoins / paper-check kill
events.desc: The digital-rails regime change: FedNow, the GENIUS stablecoin framework, the end of paper Treasury checks, the master-account gate. The current break.

leadup.label: FedNow instant-payment service goes live
leadup.note: Fed launches 24/7 real-time interbank settlement rail

leadup.label: Hagerty introduces the GENIUS Act (S.394)
leadup.note: federal stablecoin licensing framework introduced in the Senate

leadup.label: EO 14247 'Modernizing Payments' signed
leadup.note: orders Treasury to stop issuing paper checks by Sept 30, 2025

leadup.label: Senate passes the GENIUS Act 68-30
leadup.note: first chamber clears the stablecoin framework

leadup.label: House passes GENIUS & CLARITY ('Crypto Week')
leadup.note: 308-122 and 294-134 send the stablecoin bill to the president

leadup.label: Trump signs the GENIUS Act into law
leadup.note: first US federal stablecoin regulatory framework enacted

leadup.label: Treasury paper-check phase-out takes effect
leadup.note: federal disbursements move electronic-only under EO 14247

leadup.label: FDIC issues GENIUS stablecoin-issuer rules
leadup.note: proposed standards for permitted issuers (verify before load-bearing)

leadup.label: Senate Banking advances the CLARITY Act
leadup.note: broader digital-asset market-structure bill (verify before load-bearing)

entity_action.label: The current restructuring
entity_action.note: The re-founding as M&A: statutory subsidiaries dissolved, EO-only phantoms stood up. The one statutory charter = the SCRC (the OCC of the digital era). The dissolutions are real; the constructions are sand — except GENIUS.
